# Visa Imagery — Source & Attribution

**Status:** v0 ships with **palette-matched gradient placeholders** generated by `ffmpeg` from the cinematic colour tokens. Real photography must be sourced and swapped in before launch.

## What ships today

15 placeholder JPEGs in `assets/visa/img/` (desktop 1920×1080 + mobile 750×1000 per hero, plus 3 section accents). Each placeholder uses the cinematic palette appropriate to its page — e.g., `visa-umrah-hero.jpg` is a navy-to-gold radial gradient evoking Kaaba at night, not a photograph of the Kaaba.

These placeholders satisfy the page layout (the CSS hero overlay + silhouette SVGs render correctly on top of them) but they are **not** real Saudi imagery. They exist so the cinematic structure can ship without broken-image icons.

**Religious-imagery rule (from spec §3.5):** any depiction of Masjid al-Haram, the Kaaba, the Prophet's Mosque, or pilgrim crowds **must** come from Wikimedia Commons or a partner-licensed source. AI-generated and stock-composited religious imagery is not permitted.

## How to swap in real photos

For each row above:

1. Visit the source site, find a horizontal high-resolution photo (≥ 1920 px wide).
2. Confirm the licence allows commercial use.
3. Download the original.
4. Generate desktop + mobile renditions with `sips`:

```bash
cd /Users/samuel/GLOBALHIRE@ELAB
# Replace SOURCE.jpg with the downloaded file path and NAME with the file from the table
sips -Z 1920 --cropToHeightWidth 1080 1920 SOURCE.jpg --out assets/visa/img/NAME.jpg
sips -Z 1000 --cropToHeightWidth 1000 750 SOURCE.jpg --out assets/visa/img/NAME-mobile.jpg
```

5. Replace the placeholder in `assets/visa/img/` (file names must match exactly — the HTML already references them).
6. Add a row to the "Real images shipped" table below with the source URL, author, and licence.

Optional: produce AVIF + WebP renditions with `cwebp` and `avifenc` for better compression. The `<picture>` elements in the HTML already include `<source type="image/avif">` and `<source type="image/webp">` paths; if you produce them, the browser will pick the lighter format automatically.

## Hub hero video

The `/visa` hub HTML references `assets/visa/video/saudi-montage.{webm,mp4}` for a 12 s background video. **No video ships in v0** — `visa-hero-video.js` gracefully no-ops when the files 404, so the page falls back to the poster image without breaking. To add the video:

1. Source a 10–15 s Saudi-themed clip from https://www.pexels.com/videos (search "Saudi Arabia", "AlUla", "Riyadh"). Confirm licence.
2. Trim + convert with ffmpeg:

```bash
ffmpeg -i source.mp4 -ss 0 -t 12 -c:v libx264 -b:v 1500k -an -movflags +faststart assets/visa/video/saudi-montage.mp4
ffmpeg -i source.mp4 -ss 0 -t 12 -c:v libvpx-vp9 -b:v 1200k -an assets/visa/video/saudi-montage.webm
```

3. Confirm combined size ≤ 1 MB (`ls -lh assets/visa/video/`).
4. Add the source URL + author to a "Hub video" row below.
